title: A schedule or a storage event trigger for six pipelines
objective_text: Decide whether each of six pipelines starts on a schedule or on a storage event, then set the frequency, days, times and end date, or the event source, event types, folder and parameters.
scenario: Harbor Retail runs six pipelines, and each one was started by hand until now. Some need fixed times, one has to run more often than a daily schedule allows, and three should start the moment a file lands or is deleted, in Azure Blob Storage or in OneLake.

explanation: A schedule needs a start and an end date, so a schedule with no planned end gets a far end date. A daily schedule runs up to 10 times a day and hourly can't go below an hour, so a job every 30 minutes is minute-based with an interval of 30. A weekly schedule runs on the weekdays you select, up to 10 times a week, which fits two runs on five weekdays. Files that must load as they land call for a storage event trigger. Partner files in Azure Blob Storage use Azure Blob events, and BlobCreated covers new and updated blobs. Files in a lakehouse use OneLake events, with FileCreated for new files and FileDeleted for deletes. The subject filter keeps the trigger to one folder. Passing @pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName gives each run its file, and the ? handles the null value in a run started by hand.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-23: pipeline-runs (last updated 2026-09-29). Schedules take a type, frequency, start and end, and time zone. Start and end are both required and there's no open-ended schedule (the page suggests a far end date such as 2099). Up to 20 schedules per pipeline. Schedule parameter names must match. Storage event triggers choose OneLake events or Azure Blob events, pick event types, filter the Subject by folder, file name, file type and container, and pass @pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName. The ? is needed because file and folder name are null in a manual run. Interval-based schedules and run conditions are marked preview.

Checked on Learn 2026-11-23: job-scheduler (last updated 2026-05-13). Minute-based every 1 to 720 minutes, hourly every 1 to 72 hours, daily up to 10 times per day, weekly on selected weekdays up to 10 times per week. explore-fabric-onelake-events (last updated 2026-04-03) lists FileCreated (created or updated), FileDeleted, FileRenamed, FolderCreated, FolderDeleted and FolderRenamed. explore-azure-blob-storage-events (last updated 2025-12-11) says BlobCreated is raised when a blob is added or updated and BlobDeleted when one is removed.
